content: MAXIPIME, also known as cefepime hydrochloride, USP, is a semi-synthetic cephalosporin antibiotic with a broad spectrum of activity. It is designed for parenteral administration, meaning it is intended to be given via intramuscular or intravenous routes. The chemical name of cefepime hydrochloride is 1-[7-[2-carboxy-8-oxo-5-thia-1-azabicyclo[4.2.0]oct-2-en-3-yl]methyl]-1-methylpyrrolidinium chloride,72-(Z)-(O-methyloxime), monohydrochloride, monohydrate. Cefepime hydrochloride appears as a white to pale yellow powder. Each milligram of cefepime hydrochloride contains between 825 mcg and 911 mcg of cefepime (C19H24N6O5S2) on an anhydrous basis. This compound is highly soluble in water. MAXIPIME for Injection is available in dosages equivalent to 500 mg, 1 g, and 2 g of cefepime, and it is intended for intramuscular or intravenous use. The formulation of MAXIPIME is a sterile, dry mixture of cefepime hydrochloride and L-arginine. The product contains between 90% and 115% of the labeled amount of cefepime (C19H24N6O5S2). L-arginine is included in the formulation at an approximate concentration of 707 mg per gram of cefepime. Its purpose is to regulate the pH of the reconstituted solution, maintaining it within a range of 4 to 6. When MAXIPIME is freshly reconstituted, the solution typically exhibits a color that ranges from pale yellow to amber.
